cases.supplied_audit_observation: Qualified cross-author systems/kinetic showreel: distinct terminal, topology, depth-wall, chart and pipeline languages tied by violet/pink shutters and disclosure hierarchy; factual claims and compressed small text not adopted.

cases.title: Valley — procedural 3D valley film
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 作为统一3D世界与多机位叙事参考：桥/轨道/蒸汽保持空间和动作继承，至少四种视点均服务同一列车路径。头灯过曝、黑边和低多边形风格是已记录局限。

cases.title: Picsart AI Magic draft
cases.author_or_publisher: leosssvip-dot (repository maintainer; creator name not stated)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: A legible product arc: personal photo becomes a stylized portrait, then an output-format grid, then a background-removal result and CTA. Reusable mechanism: show one transformation at a time with the same phone/card frame so the product action stays easy to follow. Weakness observed: several near-black transition holds interrupt the sequence; small interface copy and fine-print claims are not readable at contact-sheet scale. This is a positive reference for transformation storytelling, not for its transition gaps or claims.

cases.title: Claude Android draft
cases.author_or_publisher: leosssvip-dot (repository maintainer; creator name not stated)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: The sequence moves from scattered thought cards to a phone UI, then to a plan screen and install CTA. Reusable mechanism: translate a headline into visible app states, keeping one warm orange panel and phone mockup as the continuity anchor. Cards and labels are readable in the 1080×1920 output. The download/rating claims are not independently verified; use the composition only, not those claims.

cases.title: ChatGPT square draft
cases.author_or_publisher: leosssvip-dot (repository maintainer; creator name not stated)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: Strong old-way/new-way story: fragmented tabs, one prompt, app-screen proof, then a high-contrast CTA. Reusable mechanism: explicitly label the problem state and the proposed state, then let product screenshots substantiate the benefit. The simple black/white/mint palette makes the CTA easy to find. Some shots hold for several seconds, but the full message remains coherent.

cases.title: TikTok feed ad draft (title inferred from visible app/CTA)
cases.author_or_publisher: leosssvip-dot (repository maintainer; creator name not stated)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: Bold high-contrast opening and a floating phone/feed mockup give the ad depth; subject and CTA are recognizable. However, the moving background, multiple phone thumbnails, category chips, and headline compete in the first shots, and download/user figures appear without a legible source. Not counted among excellent references; retain only as a layering idea after removing unsupported claims and background clutter.

cases.title: SHEIN three-look ad draft (title/product inferred from visible text)
cases.author_or_publisher: leosssvip-dot (repository maintainer; creator name not stated)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: A concise apparel product structure: model hero image → textile/detail close-up → waist-tie feature → three-look recap → product listing and store CTA. Reusable mechanism: alternate one full silhouette with a macro detail and finish on a native-looking product panel. This is visually coherent at portrait scale, though transition overlap and fine print are small. One distinct topic/output; no sibling variant counted separately.

cases.title: Video Shotcraft Gallery intro
cases.author_or_publisher: kingselyjoe / Wei Yihao (repository maintainer; copyright named in NOTICE)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: Warm gold-lit perspective panels, controlled camera orbit, and action verbs (“trace”, “orbit”, “cascade”, “materialize”) make the subject feel like a physical library. Not counted as an excellent reference because the opening/closing black holds and repeated logo outro consume a large portion of the runtime; small UI samples are difficult to read in the 720p composition. Useful only for the gold-on-dark material treatment and motion-verb chaptering.

cases.title: Ink Press AI Foundation Lab template
cases.author_or_publisher: kingselyjoe / Wei Yihao (repository maintainer; copyright named in NOTICE)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: Polished restrained system: warm paper background, editorial serif headlines, precise gold accent, and softly lit 2.5D cards that move from a research dashboard into a weekly brief and settle into a shared canvas. Reusable mechanism: change scale and perspective to turn a dense interface into one highlighted card, then return to a legible screen before the next claim. Small UI copy is texture rather than evidence; the film is about visual mood, not proof of the shown product claims.

cases.title: BrewReel three-recipe showcase demo
cases.author_or_publisher: Finderchangchang (BrewReel project author, as named on official site)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: One showcase film containing three recipe demonstrations (counted as one work, not three independent works): cards turns a support-chat premise into choice cards; quiz marks a misconception, asks a question, and reveals the answer; journey keeps a mascot moving across five changing shop stops and day/night settings. Reusable mechanisms: give each recipe a distinct color/shape grammar, and make the quiz answer visible before the vocabulary card. Body copy is small in the 1080×1920 output and the whole film is a mixed-style showcase, not a single product ad. The creator calls the tool a preview and says human review is required.

cases.title: Linear — Go All Out
cases.author_or_publisher: Zhangcan Ding, Growth Marketing at iArt.ai (source page updated 2026-10-03)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 2026-10-05 frame review: the logo-to-backlog reveal at 1–2s and issue-state symbols (5–7s) make a usable “status becomes visible” idea. However, the UI and most copy remain too dark/small through 8–16s, the headline is visibly mid-reveal/cropped around 2–4s, and the dense board montage is hard to parse at overview scale. Retain as a motion/brand comparison, not a reference-quality exemplar.

cases.title: PageOn explainer — voiceover version
cases.author_or_publisher: Zhangcan Ding, Growth Marketing at iArt.ai (source page updated 2026-10-03)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 2026-10-05 frame review: a relatable “blank slide tomorrow” problem (2–5s) turns into a numbered three-step process (10–24s: enter topic, research/write, design), then a whole-deck payoff (27–31s). The on-screen prompt and generated deck make the product mechanism concrete. The mechanism is reusable despite decorative transition panels and a long logo/end-card hold.

cases.title: Spotify — brief discovery/music product promo
cases.author_or_publisher: Zhangcan Ding, Growth Marketing at iArt.ai (source page updated 2026-10-03)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 2026-10-05 frame review: a “Discover new music” promise leads from the real-looking product home (1–3s) to one album (4–7s), then uses the album art as a full-frame visual bridge (8–9s) before “Find your rhythm” and daily mixes (10–12s). A brief recurring album/player frame links feature moments to the closing brand. This is a useful visual rhythm/product-story reference; sampled UI labels remain small.

cases.title: Notion — all-in-one workspace product promo
cases.author_or_publisher: Zhangcan Ding, Growth Marketing at iArt.ai (source page updated 2026-10-03)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 2026-10-05 frame review: the opening problem cards (“Tasks there. Wiki… somewhere?” at 1–2s) lead to the “one workspace” premise (3–5s), followed by clearly titled feature demonstrations: slash command/docs (6–9s), table-to-board (12–16s), and AI from notes to next steps (18–23s). Each headline cues a concrete UI change. The samples are clearly distinct from the page-generation explainer by using workspace consolidation and modular feature proof.

cases.title: Wise — one-shape money transfer product demo
cases.author_or_publisher: Zhangcan Ding, Growth Marketing at iArt.ai (source page updated 2026-10-03)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 2026-10-05 frame review: a distinctive single-shape logo reveal (0–2s) transitions directly to the transfer form, then sequentially shows amount/rate/fee (4–7s), recipient search (8–10s), review/confirm (11–13s), transfer tracking (15–19s), and account/card features (20–27s). Persistent green framing and interface continuity make a complex flow easy to follow. The example values and transfer-time claims are fictional/unverified and should not be copied as facts.

cases.title: Duolingo — emotional language-learning story
cases.author_or_publisher: Zhangcan Ding, Growth Marketing at iArt.ai (source page updated 2026-10-03)
cases.supplied_audit_observation: 2026-10-05 frame review: a handwritten birthday letter from Abuela frames a language barrier (“I never understood a word,” 4–6s); the phone lesson and streak growth (7–22s) visualize effort over time, then the letter is translated (23–30s) and a call connects them (32–37s). That return to the letter gives the app demo an emotional payoff rather than leaving it as a feature montage. The final logo card (39–44s) is long but clear.
